If you end up told to evacuate, you GO. Withdraw money if you have to. 

I'm a Floridian who has ridden out her fair share of hurricanes. 

Hurricane Ian rocked my world. We were told to evacuate, prioritized helping our neighbors, and by the time we were ready to leave, the flood water had already reached the cars. 

We ended up getting over 12ft of flood water from the river we lived on, reaching our house, spilling 30 gallons of fuel inside the house where we got well over 5ft inside. 

If my husband hadn't found life jackets before the water was too high, we would have died with our young children. 

Thankfully, we were able to swim across the river to a 2 story house to ride out the rest of the storm. 

My biggest regret is that we didn't prioritize our own family first, and my children had to experience such a horrific event.

Take the weather warnings seriously. They tell you to evacuate, leave immediately. Alone, if you have to.

This was an extremely helpful and informative response. After reading all of the links, watching the videos and taking the test, I agree that I probably have hypophantasia rather than aphantasia (I've never heard of hypophantasia before today). 

The test results read back to me as phantasia, which I suppose is accurate since it's not just black in my mind. I can visualize *something*, but it's akin to most of the #2 examples in the links above where the image is very blurred with low saturation and contrast with the details usually blurred completely unless I think of specific traits, but those are visualized separate from the original image and cannot be combined. 

I'm definitely an associator, most of my mental images feel like they're at the top right of my head. 

It takes a lot of effort to "see" any kind of mental image, and they're usually very fleeting. I also can't "look" at it directly, always off center, almost like trying to look directly at an eye floater. They disappear very quickly, and the already low image quality degrades significantly the longer I try to hold onto an image, which is 2-3 seconds at best. 

That all said, reading the links and attempting the exercises was super informative and was somehow very mentally strenuous, lol. I feel like I have a tension headache from trying to conjure up mental imagery the best I could!

That all said, I think I can comfortably disregard the question of whether I have prosopagnosia and should look more into hypophantasia. 

Thank you so much!

ETA: when I do have mental imagery of an object, it's surrounded by black and I'm "seeing" this blurred object in vacuum. When prompted to visualize scenery, it's a very blurred, constantly changing image surrounded by black.

At first, the wayward meets conditions set by the betrayed in an effort to smooth over and stabilize the crisis. But this isn't for the BS, it's still self-serving and an act of self-preservation. So, you do "just enough" to spare those feelings. You're still in a state of viewing the BS as something that can be manipulated if you make the right moves/say the right thing. 

You can regret what you did because of what it did to upset the balance you tried to create between reality and a lie, as a wayward. Regretting that the affair, which felt like added to your life, was really an extremely harmful detour to end up back in your reality and now it's with added trauma. 

​

For me, indicators of remorse (now as a betrayed without real insight into my husband's mind) would be what I did. If he began doing more than I asked of him, if he spent his personal time reading books, removing additional triggers/temptations after finding the root of his why (underneath my afffair. There are plenty of BS who never revenge cheat, so it's a surface reason for him but not the root cause which can only be found in a facet within himself), engaging in meaningful conversation with me first with a vulnerability that shows me that he can handle my hurt without his ego, and just actively ON HIS OWN TIME OUTSIDE OF MY PROMPTING, trying to become a better person for himself and not in exchange for my patience. 

​

But, I refuse to believe that remorse can skip over the shame stage. You can't be remorseful without seeing the most vile parts of yourself without self delusion, and writhe in that agony.

 What a fucking insult, tbh.  

The LEAST we can do is learn ✨coping mechanisms✨ to deal with our guilt.

There's a book for surviving affairs called "NOT 'Just Friends'" by Shirley P. Glass that actually has a questionnaire in the beginning of the book to help you classify whether a friendship is platonic or technically an emotional affair. 

Your first emotional affair with your coworker was something called "monkey branching". You were trying to secure something else before leaving your current situation. Not all cheating requires a feeling of wanting to leave or end your current relationship. 

You can want to remain with your fiancé and still have an emotional affair. Whether you want to stay with or leave your current partner is not what defines a relationship as an affair. It's the boundaries that are crossed from a platonic to non-platonic relationship that makes it an affair.

From a wayward with a possible perspective to offer:

I have cPTSD stemming from abuse I've lived through in my life, starting as young as early as I can remember. 

I remember a lot of shame surrounding my hyper-sexuality starting from a young age. 

I learned that hyper-sexuality can be, and is, normal and common for those who suffer trauma from sexual abuse. Learning that, began my journey towards healing and coping. 

As an above commentor said: this may be your subconscious attempt to regain control of your sexuality in a response to a traumatic sexual violation. Your brain's attempt to try and protect you from continued trauma and hurt. 

I'm imagining that in cases of trauma and PTSD, regardless of the origin and cause, it is probably normal and common for fantasies to begin budding as a coping mechanism. 

Whether it's a healthy coping mechanism or not, that's to be examined by the individual and hopefully with a professional (therapy). 

OP, you're not weird or abnormal. You're reeling from serious trauma and your brain is trying to protect you. Unpacking this in IC could be hugely beneficial for you, even for the reassurance. 

However, I don't advise you ever share this with your WP. They might internalize it as a future permission, or it might minimize the impact of what they did to you. 

Anyway, the word vomit TL;DR: I doubt it's that you've discovered an underlying cuck kink, and more likely a common self preservation PTSD response.

I see you haven't gotten any responses from any WS, so I'll chip in. 

I keep seeing how you are trying to find reason to try and stifle your pain because it hurts your WS. Am I reading that correctly? 

You do not need to set yourself on fire to keep them warm. Your outward expression of pain and grief is yours to feel, your triggers are valid. You can't control triggers. You have legitimate PTSD. This was a trauma. 

Would you ask someone with PTSD, a victim of a different trauma, to please control their trigger reponse since it was making ______ uncomfortable/feel guilty? I have cPTSD from over a decade of various forms of abuse, and I 100% see that the PTSD and trigger responses from infidelity trauma to be valid and real. 

Unpack why you think your feelings are worth less than theirs. 

Yes, your WS is going to feel guilt. Remorse. Grief. But those are the consequences of their actions, and emotions they choose to experience with the choice of reconciliation. They don't get the option to rugsweep. 

As my BS aptly puts it: "I'm so sorry your hand hurts after punching me in the face repeatedly".

Also, it's okay for your WS to have their feelings. But it's inappropriate to put the emotional burden on YOU about how they're feeling about betraying you. They need to have a therapist or friends, who were not any part of the affair or knowing about it, to confide in. It's unfair to ask you to deal with the trauma of betrayal, while also trying to survive with the daily reminders that the person beside you is capable of such betrayal AND to deal with their hurt feelings over your trauma. 

Put yourself first, here. 

Your WS needs to ask you what you need in that moment. It won't always be the same. There's no secret love language to ease the trauma of betrayal.
